output.brief: The departures are concentrated in the Kestrel review team, not the group as a whole. Eight of the eleven associates on Kestrel left, against one of thirteen others. Kestrel associates also logged about 2,270 hours a year, against about 1,940 for the rest of the group, with weekend work on 31% of weekends. Every Kestrel associate reported to Dorian Faulk, so the records cannot tell whether the workload or his supervision is the cause. Pay, the firm-wide billable target and general market mobility do not fit the pattern, since other groups barely changed. I am fairly confident the workload on Kestrel is a major driver. I am not yet confident about supervision. Do not pay a group-wide retention bonus or close the review now; it would not reach the people leaving. Next, run the confidential interviews, designed to separate workload from supervision. Consider reducing Kestrel's review load if the interviews confirm it. Add matter and supervisor fields to attrition reporting.
